summary: Iteration 16: Verified the behavior-preserving refactor of download_kyc() in /app/backend/solar_epc.py (Response return moved inside try; explicit `except HTTPException: raise`; other exceptions -> 502). Ran 9/9 GREEN pytest on backend covering (a) full KYC upload->download flow with byte-for-byte equality and Content-Disposition header, (b) 404 (not 500) for a non-existent file id, plus regressions on Solar catalog (components=11, brands>=18, seeded packages Premium Home + Value Home), estimate with brand override reflected in BOQ, brand approval RBAC (vendor pending hidden from public, vendor approve=403, admin reject empty reason=422, admin approve then public visible), customer /packages/manage=403, and freelancer enquiries contract {received, sent, unread} + mark-read flips unread to 0.
critical_code_review_comments: download_kyc() refactor is correct: `data, ct = await asyncio.to_thread(_get_object, ...)` and `return Response(...)` are inside the same try scope, so no NameError on the response path. `except HTTPException: raise` correctly propagates the 404 raised earlier for missing/unowned records, while unexpected storage failures map to 502. Verified end-to-end: uploaded PNG comes back byte-identical with inline Content-Disposition filename.

_get_object uses a retry with force=True key mint on 404 from storage — good resilience. Note it will still map a genuine storage-side 404 (after retry) to a 502 in download_kyc via requests.raise_for_status(); that is acceptable behavior (server-side data inconsistency) but consider distinguishing 'object missing' from 'storage down' for observability.

upload_kyc size limit is checked AFTER `await file.read()` — an attacker can force the server to buffer up to arbitrary UploadFile size before the 15MB check triggers. Consider streaming/chunked read or enforcing FastAPI/Starlette max_upload_size at the router level.

download_kyc accepts token via query string (`?auth=`) by mutating request.scope['headers']. This works, but tokens in query strings can leak via server access logs / referrers; if this path is only used for browser / previews consider issuing a short-lived signed URL instead.
